issues.description: Field mismatch: the Genre struct's field name is inconsistent between artifacts. The problem statement (problem_statement.md) declares that Genre should have a String property named 'name' and an optional String 'subgenre'. In the solution (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift) the struct declares the property as 'genreName' (let genreName: String). However, the solution's Client code constructs and accesses the field using 'name' (calls Genre(name: ...) and uses genre.name). This inconsistency will cause immediate compilation errors and prevents students from building or running the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the Genre struct's property from 'genreName' to 'name' to match the problem statement and the rest of the solution code. Specifically, change 'let genreName: String' to 'let name: String' in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift. This will align the struct definition with the existing initializers (Genre(name: ...)) and property accesses (genre.name).

issues.description: The concept is the name/title of a Genre. The Problem Statement (problem_statement.md) specifies the Genre has a String property called 'name'. The Solution's Genre struct (Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift) declares this property as 'genreName' (let genreName: String). Meanwhile the Solution's Client (Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift) accesses the property as 'name' (genre.name). This inconsistent identifier mapping for the same conceptual field (Genre.name vs Genre.genreName) will prevent students from mapping the requirement to the implementation and causes compilation errors in the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Genre property name consistent. Preferred: rename the Solution's Genre property from 'genreName' to 'name' (change to 'let name: String') in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift so it matches the Problem Statement and the Client usage. Alternatively, update Client access and problem text to use 'genreName', but renaming to 'name' is recommended to align artifacts and avoid student confusion.
